principles: Runtime-owned by default: local Lattice CLI owns agent prompt templates unless a project explicitly opts into local prompt assets.
Read-only first: diagnostics may classify stale assets but must not delete, repair, or migrate them in this story.
Host-neutral evidence: Claude/Codex local checks remain Non-authority and Authority completion requires verified receipts.
Consistency of logic: one projection should feed doctor/adapter/rollout surfaces instead of divergent path checks.
drivers: Existing projects may contain stale .claude/agents or .Codex/agents that shadow runtime prompts.
Default projects should not need prompt-only thin config just to use the local installed CLI.
Regression coverage must preserve B-bfb5 prompt token savings and avoid provider billing claims.

options.name: A: read-only AgentAssetResolution projection consumed by existing diagnostics
pros: Fixes the real visibility gap without mutating projects
Fits doctor/verify/rollout surfaces without arbitrary new workflow
cons: Does not automatically clean stale files; operator still needs a future explicit repair story

options.name: B: automatic migration to runtime-owned mode
pros: Would remove stale local prompt assets immediately
cons: Out of scope for current user boundary
Risky because it deletes or rewrites project-owned files
Would mix diagnostics with repair and increase correctness risk

options.name: C: keep current behavior and only document it
cons: Does not solve stale project-local prompt assets shadowing runtime prompts
Does not make token/copy risk mechanically visible
Leaves default semantics inconsistent with the runtime-owned plan

chosen: A: read-only AgentAssetResolution projection consumed by existing diagnostics
rationale: Choose the narrow read-only projection because it addresses the real correctness gap while preserving explicit repair and Authority boundaries.

preMortem.scenario: Projection incorrectly treats stale local prompts as safe runtime-owned assets
preMortem.trigger: Hash comparison only checks file existence or names, not rendered runtime content
preMortem.consequence: A project can silently keep old high-token or stale authority wording
preMortem.mitigation: Compare project-local agent files against package registry renderings for each host and mark mismatches as stale or override.

preMortem.scenario: Diagnostic starts implying Authority completion from local prompt registry checks
preMortem.trigger: Fields or prose reuse receipt/fullAuthorityDone language
preMortem.consequence: Local Non-authority evidence is overclaimed as Authority Server proof
preMortem.mitigation: Keep authority fields absent/false and include explicit boundary text in diagnostics, tests, and summary.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation becomes an arbitrary asset framework rewrite
preMortem.trigger: Adding repair/migration/deletion or broad artifact isolation beyond prompt assets
preMortem.consequence: Higher risk changes and possible user-owned file loss
preMortem.mitigation: Limit this story to read-only projection, doctor/verify/rollout display, stale detection, smokes, and token accounting.
